candidate.family: path traversal / missing containment of identifier-to-filename mapping (CWE-22)
candidate.note: Full screener record summarised here; the lead was re-verified against the pinned copy.

entry_point: Assistant-facing MCP tools (docs, memory, templates) driven by calling the real tool handlers, and the local web API's document/memory/template routes driven with httptest over the real chi router; both against temporary project folders, as the project's own tests do. No server process and no network.

verified.entry_point: Confirmed offline on the pinned copy: an MCP docs get with path '../secret' and an HTTP GET /docs/../secret (and its URL-encoded spelling) return a Markdown file outside .knowns/docs; docs update with a traversing newPath writes outside; docs delete removes outside; the imported-doc lookup resolves outside; a symlink inside docs to an outside file is followed. The memory tool reads/deletes outside with a slash-bearing id and creates outside through the review flow; promote re-uses a traversing id read from the record's own frontmatter. Template create writes outside; an import-qualified name traverses out of the imported template library; the preview's templateFile reads an arbitrary file. The injected views (memory snapshot, preview destination contents, raw doc source) do the same.

verified.project_tests_run: Pristine pinned copies of all *_test.go in internal/storage, internal/mcp/handlers and internal/server/routes are restored at grading time and run in the functional group; they pass on the pinned+injected tree and on the oracle.
verified.no_leaked_regression_tests: The published fix is the direct child of the pinned commit; its added tests (safepath/path_test.go, doc_store_test.go additions, memory_store_test.go additions, template_store_security_test.go, templates_security_test.go) are absent at the pinned commit.
verified.local_matrix: 19 security tests: 0 pass on pinned+injected, 19 pass on oracle. Functional group (23 hidden + project tests) passes on both trees. All 11 check patches apply with patch -p1 and behave as declared.

patch_checks.why: fresh agent, report + repo only; written downstream

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the reference refusal is an ordinary returned error (tool error / 4xx); a panic or 500 is not produced and would fail the same tests, while the functional suite catches any crash on legitimate use.
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the resource is exactly the file the identifier maps to; there is no proxy or neighbouring object that could be authorised instead.
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: filesystem containment has no peer or direction dimension; the read and write sides are separate tests (T2/T3), not one role toggle.
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the only normalising step before the store is URL decoding, and its output is still refused by the reference guard; a guard placed on the raw URL string would also be caught by the encoded-spelling test, but no separate patch is needed because the same security test covers it.
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: containment is purely path-based; there is no external authority that could return nothing and make the guard fail open.

traps.lever: published-fix far site (pattern A): template library, a different feature
traps.shape: template name traversal through create and through the import-qualified lookup; template-file selector traversal in the preview
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the report is about documents and memory notes; the code-generation template library is a separate feature in another package

traps.lever: published-fix far sites (pattern A): the write operations in the landing feature
traps.shape: create/rename/delete with a traversing path, including absolute and platform-separator spellings
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the observed impact is a read; create, rename and delete each build their own path and look covered by the read guard

traps.lever: landing site's shape variants (pattern A input shapes)
traps.shape: imported-doc lookup, symlink inside the library to an outside target, encoded wildcard, absolute/volume/UNC/device spellings
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a plain '..' string check fixes the reported example but misses symbolic links and platform spellings

traps.lever: landing feature's sibling: memory identifiers supplied by clients (pattern A)
traps.shape: slash-bearing ids on read, delete and review-create; trailing dot, backslash and colon spellings
traps.reason_to_dismiss: memory ids are normally generated tokens, so they look trusted and the identifier check looks unnecessary

traps.lever: published-fix far site (pattern A): save/reload path using a stored identifier
traps.shape: promote/demote of a record whose own metadata carries a traversing id
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the identifier came from our own stored file and was already used to fetch the record, so it looks validated

traps.lever: injected sibling: memory snapshot recovery view
traps.shape: snapshot read of a traversing id
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a read-only recovery view of a copy the product itself wrote; it looks like internal bookkeeping
traps.realistic_because: the surrounding tree already keeps pre-migration memory snapshots and exposes recovery operations; the helper mirrors the memory store's naming and is reached through the memory tool

traps.shape: destination derived from template actions after request-variable substitution reads outside the project
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the destination looks like template-author configuration, and the published protection above it covers the template-file read
traps.realistic_because: the preview already computes the destination and substitutes request variables into it; showing the current destination so the UI can diff the change is a natural addition in the same handler

traps.lever: injected sibling: raw document source view
traps.shape: wildcard document path rejoined to the docs root outside the store's read
traps.reason_to_dismiss: an export view for the web UI, assumed to be the same document store the report covers
traps.realistic_because: the document routes already dispatch wildcard suffixes (history, diff, restore) and the handler reads the raw file for download; it uses the same path normaliser the other routes use

out_of_scope_notes: CWE-306 suggested by the advisory (local HTTP/MCP server without auth) is not pursued.
The template code-generation engine joins template-author-configured source paths (internal/codegen) and is CLI-only; different sink, not pursued.
The project's own import routes already validate their names at the pinned commit; not part of this task.
